recheck.evidence_quote: All requests require an API key in the x-api-key header (search-result excerpt of the vendor's FanBasis/fbnewapi GitHub docs; page itself not fetchable)
recheck.notes: NOT fully settled. Vendor docs exist: FanBasis (rebranded "Commas") has a GitHub repo FanBasis/fbnewapi and a docs site commasdocs.com titled "Commas API Reference". Neither could be read: www.fanbasis.com/public-api/ and docs.fanbasis.com/llms.txt returned 403, the GitHub repo and raw files returned 404, commasdocs.com is JS-rendered and returned only a title, and support.fanbasis.com failed on SSL. Verified only via search-result excerpts: REST-style API at https://www.fanbasis.com/public-api/, API key in the x-api-key header, and a third-party copy suggesting keys are scoped (checkout-sessions, payments, webhooks, customers). A fanbasis.com marketing page lists "APIs and SDKs" under "Enterprise & APIs", which could mean plan or sales gating. Inferred, not verified: that keys are self-serve from the dashboard. Where to create a key, plan requirements, rate limits and the endpoint list are all unconfirmed. I set access to self_serve_free as the best guess, but it is low confidence, and approval_required or paid_plan can't be ruled out. Do not use no_public_api, since public docs do exist. Recommend someone with a FanBasis account check the dashboard for an API Keys page, or the docs be viewed in a browser.
